memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Look,' he said, 'the sun is still high; it is not time for the flocks to be gathered. Water the sheep and take them back to pasture.' 'We can't,' they replied, 'until all the flocks are gathered and the stone has been rolled away from the mouth of the well. Then we will water the sheep.' While he was still talking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, for she was a shepherd. When Jacob saw Rachel daughter of his uncle Laban, and Laban's sheep, he went over and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle's sheep. Then Jacob kissed Rachel and began to weep aloud. He had told Rachel that he was a relative of her father and a son of Rebekah. So she ran and told her father." - Gen 29:7-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When Rachel arrives, something in Jacob springs to life. He single-handedly rolls away the large stone — a job that normally waited for several shepherds — waters her flock, and then, overcome with emotion, kisses his cousin and weeps aloud. These are not tears of sadness but of relief and joy. After the loneliness of his flight, the fear and the stone-pillow nights, Jacob has finally found family. He belongs somewhere again.

There is something deeply human here. Jacob had been a stranger and a fugitive, cut off from everyone he knew. Now, at this well, he is embraced back into a family. The weight of his isolation breaks, and it pours out in tears.

Many of us know that ache of loneliness — the longing to belong, to be known, to find our people. God understands that longing; He made us for connection, and He does not intend for us to walk through life utterly alone (Gen 2:18).

Even more, God draws His people into a family through Christ. Those who come to Him are no longer strangers but members of God's household (Eph 2:19), brothers and sisters in His family. If you feel like an outsider today, remember: in Christ there is a place where you belong. God brings the lonely into a home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I know the ache of longing to belong?
2. How has God provided family and belonging in my life?
3. Have I embraced my place in God's family through Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You know my longing to belong and be known. Thank You that in Christ I am no longer a stranger but part of Your family. Draw the lonely into Your home. Amen.
